subject: Problems turning digitsurface result into an array in order to perform GPA

messages.author: 37aef82572a5ce5d
messages.subject: Problems turning digitsurface result into an array in order to perform GPA
parts:
Hello,


I am a researcher attempting to compare thyroid cartilage (in PLY format) from two different rodent specimens. I am a novice to R, so I have been attempting to learn as much as I can from the geomorph manual and the forum here.


I have been able to define homologous landmarks, create a template, and perform the digitsurface function all without issue. My problem comes when I try to turn the digitsurface results into an array (which I believe is needed to perform the gpagen function.


After viewing the coordinates of the LMM2 array, the data appears scattered and no longer resembles the thyroid shape. Can anyone give me a clue to why this is happening, if I am completing the array function incorrectly, or if there is another way to perform the GPA without having to turn the data into an array?



If anyone can give me some more information on what I am doing wrong or any other way to perform the GPA while still maintaining the thyroid shape in order to normalize the data and compare with other thyroid shapes, please share with me. I have attached images detailing the steps I have taken and below is the code I have used:



LMM2<-read.ply("LMM2-Thyroid.ply") #read LMM2 ply file (3D surface of thyroid cartilage for specimen 1)

LMM3<-read.ply("LMM3_Thyroid.ply") #read LMM3 ply file (3D surface of thyroid cartilage for specimen 2)


a<-digit.fixed(LMM3,40) #manually place landmarks on the 3D surface in a line along the contour you want to capture

LMdata<-digitsurface(LMM2, a, ptsize=1, center=TRUE) #digitize surface of LMM2 using the fixed landmark data specified on LMM3


LMM2LM<-readland.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result

X<-LMM2LM[,,] #turn data into an array

LMM2Array<-arrayspecs(X,140,3) #specifications of array

 

plotAllSpecimens(LMM2Array)



Thank you for any information you can provide.

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Problems turning digitsurface result into an array in order to perform GPA
parts:
Heather,

 

Try plotAllSpecimens(LMM2LM) to see what it looks like.  This is the original data read in by readland.nts and should already be in the form of a 3D array.

 

The additional steps you had included, turning this into an array, and then into a 3D array, are unnecessary, and are likely where your problem has arisen.

 

Dean

Hello,

 

I am a researcher attempting to compare thyroid cartilage (in PLY format) from two different rodent specimens. I am a novice to R, so I have been attempting to learn as much as I can from the geomorph manual and the forum here.

 

I have been able to define homologous landmarks, create a template, and perform the digitsurface function all without issue. My problem comes when I try to turn the digitsurface results into an array (which I believe is needed to perform the gpagen function.

 

After viewing the coordinates of the LMM2 array, the data appears scattered and no longer resembles the thyroid shape. Can anyone give me a clue to why this is happening, if I am completing the array function incorrectly, or if there is another way to perform the GPA without having to turn the data into an array?

 

 

If anyone can give me some more information on what I am doing wrong or any other way to perform the GPA while still maintaining the thyroid shape in order to normalize the data and compare with other thyroid shapes, please share with me. I have attached images detailing the steps I have taken and below is the code I have used:

 

 

LMM2<-read.ply("LMM2-Thyroid.ply") #read LMM2 ply file (3D surface of thyroid cartilage for specimen 1)

LMM3<-read.ply("LMM3_Thyroid.ply") #read LMM3 ply file (3D surface of thyroid cartilage for specimen 2)

 

a<-digit.fixed(LMM3,40) #manually place landmarks on the 3D surface in a line along the contour you want to capture

LMdata<-digitsurface(LMM2, a, ptsize=1, center=TRUE) #digitize surface of LMM2 using the fixed landmark data specified on LMM3

 

LMM2LM<-readland.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result

X<-LMM2LM[,,] #turn data into an array

LMM2Array<-arrayspecs(X,140,3) #specifications of array

 

plotAllSpecimens(LMM2Array)

 

 

Thank you for any information you can provide.

Thank you, that has fixed my issue of visualizing the digitsurface result.

My reasoning for turning the data into a 3D array was because I am having problems with the gpagen function.
If I use LMM2LM, I get the error:

Error in nu || nv : invalid 'x' type in 'x || y'

and if I use LMM2Array, the function works, but I have the same problem of seeing the coordinates as scattered, not resembling any shape.
I have tried this with and without defining the curves in the gpagen function.
Is there a key step I am missing or am I using the wrong variable in the gpagen function?
a<-digit.fixed(LMM3,40) #manually place landmarks on the 3D surface in a line along the contour you want to capture
template<-buildtemplate(LMM3,a,100) # build a template of specimen LMM3 using fixed landmarks
LMdata<-digitsurface(LMM2, a, ptsize=1, center=TRUE) #digitize surface of LMM2 using the fixed landmark data specified on LMM3

#fuction automatically pulls the template you created previously

c<-define.sliders(a,20) #make the slider matrix needed for gpagen (GPA) function

LMM2LM<-readland.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result
X<-LMM2LM[,,] #turn data into an array
LMM2Array<-arrayspecs(X,140,3) #specifications of array

Y.GPA<-gpagen(LMM2LM, curves=c, surfaces=NULL, PrinAxes=TRUE, max.iter=NULL, ProcD=TRUE, Proj=TRUE, print.progress=TRUE)
#Perform GPA on data from digitsurface

plotAllSpecimens(Y.GPA$coords)
plotAllSpecimens(LMM2LM)

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Problems turning digitsurface result into an array in order to perform GPA
parts:
Dear Heather,

As Dean said, there's no reason you should be taking those additional steps, and as such you are making it more difficult for yourself.

But also there's a simple solution to why you are having trouble: you are using the wrong function

You are reading in a single .nts file at line
LMM2LM<-readland.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result

using the wrong function. The function you need is readmulti.nts. The two functions are different - they read different types of NTS files; the former a single NTS file containing coordinate data for multiple specimens, and the latter for single NTS files each containing coordinate data for a single specimen.  (I have updated the help pages for these two functions in geomorph 3.0.4 coming very soon to CRAN to hopefully make this extra clear).

Anyway, if you do:
LMM2LM<-readmulti.nts("LMM2.nts") #reads the digitized surface result
You'll end up with LMM2LM being a 3D array, containing a single specimen

Emma

parts:
Hello again,

I am having trouble finding the right function to digitize semilandmarks along the boundary of a thyroid.
After defining 6 fixed points with digit.fixed function, I want to place equidistant semilandmarks between these landmarks and along the boundary curve, but I am having difficulties finding the function to do so. I am following examples in geomorph and can't get the right result.
Code:
LMM3<-read.ply("LMM3_Thyroid.ply") #read LMM3 ply file

a<-digit.fixed(LMM3,6) #manually place landmarks on the 3D surface
c<-digit.curves(a[1,],a,15,closed=FALSE) #calculates equidistant semilandmarks along a curve

plot(a)
points(c)

##################
Do I use function (digit.curves) to place equidistant landmarks between each set of fixed landmarks (run the function for each pair of landmarks) or is there another way? Also, is there a function to place semilandmarks along a boundary curve of a specimen between two fixed landmarks?
I apologize for the excessive questions, but I have been reading the geomorph manual and through various publications and have not been able to figure this out.

Thank you,
Heather

messages.subject: Re: Problems turning digitsurface result into an array in order to perform GPA
parts:
Dear Heather,

The way I would do this is to manually place lots of fixed landmarks along the curve you are looking at, and then use the digit.curves function to take those landmark coordinates (as a matrix) and resample them as equidistant semilandmarks. This is the same this as what is done in tpsDIG2 with 2D curves - the user marks out the curve by hand, and the software places equidistant semilandmarks along the curve. So the same, you just have to run two functions, one after the other.

Emma
